# Egress redaction gateway (`dsh-redact-gateway`)
English | 中文

> DSH sends prompts, tool results and attachments to a model provider **verbatim**.
> This plugin in

tercepts each request before it leaves the machine, replaces
> identity numbers, phone numbers, bank

cards, emails, addresses, customer names
> and secrets with numbered placeholders, sends the masked

copy, then restores
> the response. The user reads the original text; the model never saw it.

Built for small teams that must hand internal documents, code and customer data
to a cloud model, wh

ere the security review stops at exactly one question: *does
our data leave?* Unlike "a redaction to

ol the model has to remember to call",
this enforces itself at the transport boundary — the model ha

s no choice and
there is no "forgot to call it" failure mode.
## 1. What it actually does
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Three properties follow:

1. **The model side cannot be bypassed.** The interception point is the
`llm/stream` waterfall, not

a tool. Every model call — main conversation,
subagents, session titles, compaction — passes through

it.
2. **The user side is lossless.** The session log keeps originals; placeholders
exist only in t

he outbound copy. Restoration needs no guessing and no history
rewriting.
3. **It is auditable.** Ev

ery substitution writes one record with category, rule,
placeholder, partial mask, keyed fingerprint

, and a hash-chain link. Editing or
deleting a line breaks `verify`.
### This is pseudonymisation, not anonymisation

Placeholders are reversible and the mapping lives on this machine, so under PIPL
Art. 73 this is **去

标识化 (pseudonymisation)**, not 匿名化 (anonymisation): the
mapping is still personal data and stays in s

cope. The plugin provides PIPL
Art. 51 technical measures (encryption, de-identification, access con

trol); it is
**not** an exemption from personal-data obligations. Do not describe it as
anonymisatio
n in a security review.
## 2. Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then open **Settings → Egress redaction gateway** to see state, switch modes,
toggle categories, and

export the audit CSV. The plugin row's own configuration
lives in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`

audit CSV. The plugin row's own configuration
lives in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (section 5).

> After installing, send one message containing test data (for example a made-up
> phone number) and

confirm the counter on the settings page increases. A counter
> that stays at zero means intercepti
on is not active — investigate before use.
## 3. What it detects
| Category | Placeholder | Validation | Main false-positive risk |
| `secret` | `[SECRET_1]` | vendor prefixes + entropy + keyword proximity | hashes/UUIDs (built-in a

llowlist) |
| `idcard` | `[IDCARD_1]` | GB 11643 ISO 7064 MOD 11-2 + real date + division code | 18-

digit order numbers |
| `bankcard` | `[BANKCARD_1]` | Luhn + major IIN ranges | Luhn-valid order num

bers/IMEIs |
| `phone` | `[PHONE_1]` | prefix + boundaries | rare |
| `email` | `[EMAIL_1]` | practi

cal regex + structure checks | rare |
| `address` | `[ADDR_1]` | province/city/district + road + doo

r number | addresses in legal/news text |
| `name` | `[NAME_1]` | surname table + context anchoring

(strict by default) | bare matching would flag "张总" (off by default) |
| `org` | `[ORG_1]` | GB 3210

0 unified social credit code + name suffixes | common words ("建设", "东方") |
| `custom` | `[TERM_1]` |
literal, longest match | very short terms |

**Priority / overlap**: `secret > custom > idcard > bankcard > phone > email >
org > address > name`

. The eleven digits inside an ID card are never also read as
a phone number.

**The custom dictionary is the highest-ROI switch.** Put customer lists, project
codenames and inter

nal product names in `dictionary` (or let the agent add them
with `redact_dictionary`). It is far mo

re reliable than any heuristic for names
and organizations.
### Placeholder format

The default is `[EMAIL_1]` — single brackets, upper-case category, underscore,
incrementing number.

A measured round-trip study (arXiv:2610.34012) found this
shape survives best: models rewrite `<Name

_1>` into `[Name_1]` themselves, and
`[[…]]` collides with wiki-link syntax.

Rehydration is **tolerant**: `[[EMAIL_1]]`, `[ email - 1 ]`, `［EMAIL_1］`,
`(EMAIL_1)` and `{EMAIL_1}

` all restore, and are counted as repairs. Placeholders
the model **invents** (an `[ORG_9]` that was

never issued) are never guessed at —
they pass through untouched and are counted, which is the only

re never guessed at —
they pass through untouched and are counted, which is the only safe behaviour.
## 4. Workspace allowlists and exemptions

Matching is **longest-prefix** on the session's working directory, so a nested
directory can re-enab
le redaction inside an exempted tree.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`policy`: `enforce` (default), `audit` (record only, no substitution), `bypass`
(skip entirely, not
even an audit line).
## 8. Failure policy: why the default is "block"

If the redaction path itself fails (disk unwritable, encryption error, detector
throw), `onError: bl

ock` fails **that request** — not one byte of the original is
sent — and the error names the gateway

t request** — not one byte of the original is
sent — and the error names the gateway as the blocker.

That is the correct default for a security product: "protection failed, so the
data went out anyway"

is no protection. The cost is the occasional opaque error.
Diagnose with the `redact-gateway:` pref

ix in the DSH log; setting `onError: pass`
temporarily lets requests through (still audited), but re

storing it must be
treated as a required follow-up.

A second hard stop: **the mapping must be durable before dispatch.** If the
mapping cannot be writte

n, the request is blocked — a placeholder that leaves
without its mapping can never be restored, and

the user would be left reading
`[EMAIL_1]`.
